claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
ALD can produce a dense alumina coating a few micrometres thick or less on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited alumina coating will remain protective and adherent during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
The alumina layer will act as a diffusion barrier to oxygen ingress.
Impeding oxygen diffusion will reduce oxygen uptake and internal oxidation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Applying the coating as a surface treatment will not alter the alloy's bulk microstructure.
The alloy's bulk microstructure is responsible for its useful mechanical properties.
Alumina-coated HfNbTaTiZr will show significantly lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated material after up to 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
Alumina-coated HfNbTaTiZr will show a smaller oxide penetration depth than uncoated material after high-temperature air exposure.
After oxidation exposure, coated HfNbTaTiZr will retain room-temperature tensile ductility similar to untreated cast alloy.
After oxidation exposure, coated HfNbTaTiZr will retain high-temperature yield strength similar to untreated cast alloy at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Coating effectiveness depends on depositing a defect-free layer and maintaining adhesion during thermal cycling.
Surface roughness can affect the efficacy and adhesion integrity of the ALD alumina coating.
Thermal cycling may compromise the alumina coating's performance.
